title: Normalize tables, taxonomy, identifiers, and structured source labels
design:
2026-10-10 DESIGN (Claude Captain, main 52e7e19b). Lane A, profile rules-clause-complete. Normalization is consumer-driven (ADR 0020: no corpus-wide schema mandate); every owned registry row gets a repair or an explicit disposition.
R1 MADNESS DURATIONS (opus:F-16): table:short-term-madness / long-term-madness / indefinite-madness carry only d100+effect columns; the durations are printed in rule:madness-effects ('subjected to an effect from the Short-Term Madness table for 1d10 minutes', long-term '1d10 x 10 hours', indefinite 'lasts until cured'). Project a duration field on each table record from that source sentence (verbatim-derived values, e.g. {dice:'1d10', unit:'minute'} / {dice:'1d10', multiplier:10, unit:'hour'} / {kind:'until-cured'}), with provenance to the rule record; validate in kindSchemas. Check consumers of these tables first.
R2 TACK/HARNESS/DRAWN VEHICLES + BARDING (sol:CAP-013): equipment records for saddles, saddlebags, carriage, cart, chariot, sled, wagon (and barding/feed/stabling if present) are category 'gear' with no grouping, though the SRD prints them in the 'Tack, Harness, and Drawn Vehicles' table. Project the printed group (e.g. subcategory 'tack-harness-drawn-vehicles') for exactly the rows of that source table (population from the table itself, not a hand list), and project the Barding rule ('Barding is armor designed to protect an animal's head, neck, chest, and body. Any type of armor shown on the Armor table can be purchased as barding. The cost is four times the equivalent armor made for humanoids, and it weighs twice as much.') as a typed transformation on the barding row/record ({costMultiplier:4, weightMultiplier:2, appliesTo:'armor-table'}). Check consumers (equipment catalog, creation equipment) first; stop if a deterministic consumer changes behavior.
R3 EMPTY CELLS (fable:F6): 484 cells are '' and 88 are an em dash. Determine against the vendored PDF whether each form matches the printed cell (blank vs em dash). If they faithfully reflect two different printed forms, disposition accepted with that evidence (no consumer is harmed by the distinction); if any '' is a lost printed dash (or vice versa), repair at the extractor and add an invariant.
R4 F-10 advancement-qualifiers ('Advancement scaling qualifiers are preserved'): identify the printed scaling qualifiers the row concerns (class/feature progression text such as 'at 5th level (2d6)', 'when you reach N level', cantrip damage scaling) by inspecting progression/scaling projections and the registry provenance; repair any qualifier lost in a projection, or disposition with evidence.
R5 DISPOSITIONS: F-34 damage-field-shape ({dice} vs flat {amount}) - both shapes validated (kindSchemas validateDamageEntry) and represent two printed forms; disposition accepted/narrowed unless a consumer is harmed. F-14 choice-identifiers - check choices[].id and options ids for uniqueness/stable catalog refs across records with a real consumer (creation/level-up); repair inconsistencies or disposition. F-13 proficiency-grants - saves/skills/armor typed by eshyra-olc5.7 (PR #642, consumed by proficiencyGrants.ts); weapon/tool/language grants stay free text (no consumer); narrow accordingly.
EVIDENCE: one new test file with exact source-backed assertions for R1/R2 and generalized checks where a population exists (R2 membership equals the source table's rows; R3 if repaired). Registry rows updated with reasoning. No per-record test proliferation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each finding-registry row owned here is repaired or explicitly dispositioned under ADR 0020 section 7 (retirement names its replacing responsibility and hides no source defect): madness-durations, advancement-qualifiers, equipment-taxonomy, table-empty-cells, damage-field-shape, choice-identifiers, proficiency-grants.
- Source losses are repaired against source evidence: table durations, optional qualifiers, and Tack/Harness/Drawn Vehicles grouping and the Barding transformation survive projection; a dropped qualifier fails the build.
- Normalization items (single empty-cell form, one damage-amount shape, catalog-typed tool/skill/language/proficiency identifiers) are repaired where a named consumer or a faithful reading of the source is harmed; no corpus-wide normalization mandate without a consumer (ADR 0020: no repository-wide replacement schema).
- Synthesized headers/labels presented as source quotation are owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1 item 5, not re-implemented here.
notes:
Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.
ADR-0020 disposition pass 2026-09-22 (eshyra-o9bd.19 rebaseline): RESHAPED. The 2026-09-10 reconciliation never reached this bead; its operative acceptance still mandated corpus-wide normalization (one damage shape corpus-wide; catalog identifiers with no free-text fallback; one empty-cell form) with no named consumer. Rewritten so every owned registry finding still requires a repair or an explicit disposition (nothing is dropped), while normalization is consumer-driven. Synthesized-header flagging moved to eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1 item 5 (table:scrying-save-modifiers carries invented 'Basis'/'Circumstance' headers).
